Rebuild note: the graph format changed, so the first start after the upgrade builds each tree once.

## Calls are linked only where the code says so

- **A method on a value of unknown type is a guess.** `x.is_empty()` linked to the one tree method of that name, in whatever crate or package it lived; `cycles` and `check_architecture` then reported cycles and violations the build system rules out. Such a call is now `ambiguous`, so the `inferred` floor of `cycles` and of `deny` rules no longer sees it. `impact`, `find_callers` and `affected_tests` still include it.
- **A known type outside the tree holds its own methods.** `labels.get()` with `labels: HashMap` no longer links to a tree `get`. A type in the tree is followed strictly, and a Rust method is found in every `impl` of its type, wherever the crate puts it.
- **Rust:** `use crate::…`, `super::…` and `self::…` (lists and aliases included) scope a call to the file they name, so an imported function is `inferred` rather than `ambiguous`. A path keeps all its segments, so `std::fs::read_dir` never names the tree, and a path is never read as a value of the same name. `f(x).g()` names no receiver; `Variant(x)` and `TupleStruct(x)` are no calls. A name bound to a field (`let bank = &mut self.data;`) or a loop over fields of one type takes that type.
- A placeholder reached from several languages links only into one of them.

## Tools

- **`detect_changes`** lists definitions the change removed or renamed (`removed_symbols`) and every definition still calling one (`risk.dangling_callers`), which raises the risk to high; `affected_tests` takes those callers as seeds. All definitions of a new, untracked file count as changed.
- **`affected_tests`** lists a production helper named `test_*` only where a runner collects tests by name (Python, Ruby); elsewhere the path or a test attribute decides.
- **`find_unused`** no longer counts a local of the same name (`let x = …`) as a use, and leaves out methods of a Rust `impl Trait for Type`.
- **`explain_node`** names the same callers as `find_callers`, once each; its similar definitions come without placeholders and most alike first.
- The `cycles` description states its real default.

## Servers

- A backend reached at the moment it ends no longer drops the client that just connected.
- `--linger` and `--sleep-after` are checked before a backend starts; an edited language rule file, and a rebuilt binary of the same version, get a backend of their own.

## Releases

- Each release is now published to the MCP registry by the release workflow.

## Install

- Homebrew: `brew install attackwave/glasir/glasir`
- Scoop: add the bucket `Attackwave/scoop-glasir`, then run `scoop install glasir`
